evidence: Synthetic Windows executable under Wine on macOS; dedicated VirtualAlloc data page
checks: Target write fault records exact fault address, instruction/context RIP and thread, then original write completes.
Neighbor write wins without claiming target publication.
Cancel restores write access and leaves no capture.
Originally read-only page refuses without changing protection.
16 event-released concurrent writer threads all complete; one record retained.
Non-access exceptions and software-raised read/foreign-page access exceptions reach a later handler.
Ordinary reads do not trigger; subsequent writes do not replace the first record.
limitations: No live game page, handler ordering or startup publication observed.
Dedicated allocated page retained through process exit; heap-page ownership and concurrent protection changes excluded.
Concurrent fixture is one schedule, not a proof of all races or freedom from handler stalls.
Protection restoration failures and timeout-cancellation races were not fault-injected.
Instruction context is captured before the faulting write completes; publication semantics remain unknown.
Module and handler remain present until process exit; no unload proof.
